scope: Proposition 4.2 (Probability of good data) of the manuscript “Quantum Depletion for Fixed Bounded Repulsive Potentials” (preprints/Quantum-Depletion-for-Fixed-Bounded-Repulsive-Potentials-October-5-2026/fixed-repulsion-quantum-depletion.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 267 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 808cf0e274a8852c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The constants in the preceding definitions can be chosen so that P(z is bad) ≤ CxD−1−1/8 , P(every site in A is bad) ≤ p|A| (A ⊂ L), P(full-path bounds fail in a fixed neighborhood) ≤ CxD−6 . (4.10) In the second line p > 0 may be any sufficiently small fixed number, after increasing the threshold for D. The constants and thresholds are uniform in the position of the neighborhood and in the volume.
